duas.why: The dua of Ādam and Ḥawwā' — 'Rabbanā ẓalamnā anfusanā' — the foundational prayer of repentance for wronging oneself and begging forgiveness and mercy.
The dua of Dhun-Nūn (Yūnus) inside the whale — 'Lā ilāha illā anta subḥānaka innī kuntu min aẓ-ẓālimīn' — the most famous dua of distress and turning back to Allah in repentance.
'Rabbanā innanā āmannā faghfir lanā dhunūbanā' — the believers asking forgiveness of their sins and protection from the Fire.
'Rabbanā ighfir lanā dhunūbanā wa isrāfanā fī amrinā' — asking forgiveness for sins and excesses, and steadfastness.
'Rabbanā lā tajʿalnā fitnatan… waghfir lanā' — Ibrāhīm's people asking Allah's forgiveness and protection from being a trial.
Sayyid al-Istighfār — the master of seeking forgiveness, 'Allāhumma anta rabbī lā ilāha illā anta…', Bukhārī 6306; the most authoritative Prophetic dua of repentance.
'Ihdinā aṣ-ṣirāṭ al-mustaqīm' — from al-Fātiḥah, the central daily prayer for guidance to the straight path.
'Rabbanā lā tuzigh qulūbanā baʿda idh hadaytanā' — asking Allah not to let hearts deviate after guidance, and to grant mercy.
'Rabbanā innanā samiʿnā munādiyan yunādī lil-īmān… faghfir lanā' — responding to the call to faith and asking forgiveness and a righteous death.
'Rabbanā lā tu'ākhidhnā in nasīnā aw akhṭa'nā…' — the closing dua of al-Baqarah for forgiveness, ease of burden, and victory over disbelief.
'Yā Muqallib al-qulūb, thabbit qalbī ʿalā dīnik' — the Prophet's frequent dua asking the Turner of Hearts to keep his heart firm on the religion, Tirmidhī 3522.
The dua of Sulaymān — 'Rabbi awziʿnī an ashkura niʿmataka…' — asking Allah to inspire him to be grateful for His blessings and to do righteous deeds He is pleased with.
'Rabbi awziʿnī an ashkura niʿmataka allatī anʿamta ʿalayya wa ʿalā wālidayya' — gratitude for Allah's favor on oneself and one's parents, with repentance and submission.
Ibrāhīm's dua — 'Rabbi ijʿalnī muqīma aṣ-ṣalāti wa min dhurriyyatī' — asking to be established in prayer, a prayer of thankful devotion.
'Rabbanā ighfir lī wa liwālidayya wa lil-mu'minīn' — Ibrāhīm asking forgiveness for himself, his parents, and the believers on the Day of Reckoning.
The dua of ʿIbād ar-Raḥmān — 'Rabbanā hab lanā min azwājinā… wa ijʿalnā lil-muttaqīna imāmā' — asking to be made leaders of the God-conscious.
'Ḥasbunā Allāhu wa niʿma al-wakīl' — the declaration of total reliance on Allah, spoken by the believers when threatened; the essence of tawakkul.
The believer of Firʿawn's people — 'Wa ufawwiḍu amrī ilā Allāh' — entrusting one's whole affair to Allah in sincere submission.
'Rabbanā ʿalayka tawakkalnā wa ilayka anabnā wa ilayka al-maṣīr' — Ibrāhīm's declaration of trust, turning back, and return to Allah alone.
The dua of Āsiya, wife of Firʿawn — 'Rabbi ibni lī ʿindaka baytan fī al-jannah wa najjinī…' — the model of sincere devotion, choosing nearness to Allah over worldly power.
Ṭālūt's army: 'rabbanā afrigh ʿalaynā ṣabran wa thabbit aqdāmanā' — pour patience on us and make our feet firm; the classic dua for steadfastness in hardship.
Dua of the earlier prophets' followers: 'rabbanaghfir lanā dhunūbanā... wa thabbit aqdāmanā' — forgiveness plus firmness of feet and victory over adversity.
The magicians of Firʿawn under threat of execution: 'rabbanā afrigh ʿalaynā ṣabran wa tawaffanā muslimīn' — patience under persecution and dying in submission.
Close of al-Baqarah: '...wa-ṣbir ʿalaynā' asking God not to burden us beyond capacity and to grant endurance, pardon, mercy and support.
Dua of Dhun-Nūn (Yūnus) inside the fish: 'lā ilāha illā anta subḥānaka innī kuntu min aẓ-ẓālimīn' — the most famous dua for lifting distress and grief.
Dua of Ayyūb (Job) in illness and loss: 'annī massaniya aḍ-ḍurru wa anta arḥamu ar-rāḥimīn' — patience through affliction and appeal to God's mercy.
Yaʿqūb in his grief over Yūsuf: 'innamā ashkū baththī wa ḥuznī ilā Allāh' — turning one's sorrow and anguish to God alone.
Duʿāʾ al-Karb (Prophet's supplication for distress): 'Lā ilāha illā-llāhu al-ʿAẓīmu al-Ḥalīm...' — Bukhārī 6345 & Muslim 2730, said at times of overwhelming worry.
Response of the believers when warned of enemy armies: 'ḥasbunā Allāhu wa niʿma al-wakīl' — sufficiency of God and trust that dispels fear.
'rabbanā lā tuzigh qulūbanā baʿda idh hadaytanā' — steadfast heart and mercy so faith does not waver under pressure.
The believers among Mūsā's people: 'ʿalā Allāhi tawakkalnā rabbanā lā tajʿalnā fitnatan lil-qawmi aẓ-ẓālimīn' — reliance and courage before oppressors.
Mūsā before confronting Firʿawn: 'rabbi-shraḥ lī ṣadrī wa yassir lī amrī' — expanding the chest and easing the task, the dua for courage in daunting moments.
'rabbi zidnī ʿilman' — the dua for increase in beneficial knowledge, which the Qur'an ties to hearts finding rest through remembrance.
Dua of ʿibād ar-Raḥmān: 'rabbanā hab lanā min azwājinā wa dhurriyyātinā qurrata aʿyunin' — coolness of the eyes and tranquility through family.
'a-lā bi-dhikri-llāhi taṭmaʾinnu al-qulūb' — hearts find their peace and assurance in the remembrance of God; the anchor verse for inner calm.
Prophet's dua against anxiety and grief: 'Allāhumma innī aʿūdhu bika mina al-hammi wal-ḥazan...' — Bukhārī 6369, seeking refuge from worry, sorrow, and the burdens that weigh on the heart.
Rabbi a'ūdhu bika min hamazāt ash-shayāṭīn — Mūmināt seeking refuge in Allah from the whisperings/incitements of the devils; a direct plea for spiritual protection from the unseen.
Wa a'ūdhu bika Rabbi an yaḥḍurūn — continuation: seeking refuge lest the devils be present; pairs with 23:97 as protection from the unseen.
Sūrat al-Falaq — 'Qul a'ūdhu bi-Rabbil-falaq' — one of the two Mu'awwidhatān, the classic refuge from all created evil, darkness, and envy.
Sūrat an-Nās — 'Qul a'ūdhu bi-Rabbin-nās' — the second Mu'awwidhah, refuge from the whisperer (al-waswās) among jinn and mankind.

A'ūdhu bi-kalimāti-llāhi at-tāmmāti min sharri mā khalaq — 'I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He created' (Muslim 2708); Prophetic refuge from every harm at day's end / when stopping at a place.

Ḥasbunallāhu wa ni'mal-wakīl — 'Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs' — said by the believers when threatened by armies; the ultimate declaration of reliance for protection.
Rabbanā-ghfir lanā dhunūbanā... wa-nṣurnā 'alal-qawmil-kāfirīn — plea for forgiveness, firm footing, and victory/protection against hostile people.
Ḥasbiyallāhu lā ilāha illā huwa 'alayhi tawakkaltu — 'Allah is sufficient for me... upon Him I rely' — Prophetic verse of reliance; recited morning and evening for protection.

Bismillāhi-lladhī lā yaḍurru ma'a-smihi shay'un fil-arḍi wa lā fis-samā' — 'In the name of Allah, with whose name nothing on earth or in heaven can cause harm' (Abū Dāwūd 5088, Tirmidhī 3388); morning/evening shield from harm.
Lā ilāha illā anta subḥānaka innī kuntu min aẓ-ẓālimīn — the du'ā of Dhun-Nūn (Yūnus) from within the whale; the great supplication for rescue from distress and darkness.
Rabbanā lā taj'alnā fitnatan lil-qawmiẓ-ẓālimīn — the believers with Mūsā asking not to be made a trial/prey for the oppressing people; refuge from persecution.
Wa najjinā bi-raḥmatika minal-qawmil-kāfirīn — 'and save us by Your mercy from the disbelieving people'; direct plea for deliverance, pairs with 10:85.
Wa ufawwiḍu amrī ila-llāh, inna-llāha baṣīrun bil-'ibād — the believer of Pharaoh's family entrusting his affair to Allah for protection amid threat.
Rabbanā afrigh 'alaynā ṣabran wa thabbit aqdāmanā wa-nṣurnā 'alal-qawmil-kāfirīn — Ṭālūt's soldiers before Jālūt (Goliath) asking for patience, firmness, and victory/protection.

topics.name: Security of Home, Family & the Hereafter

duas.why: Rabbanā ātinā fid-dunyā ḥasanah wa fil-ākhirati ḥasanah wa qinā 'adhāban-nār — the comprehensive du'ā asking for good in both worlds and protection ('qinā') from the Fire.
Rabbanā hab lanā min azwājinā wa dhurriyyātinā qurrata a'yun — 'Ibād ar-Raḥmān asking for spouses and offspring who are a comfort; protection and safety for the family.
Rabbi-bni lī 'indaka baytan fil-jannah wa najjinī min Fir'awn... — Āsiyah's du'ā for a house in Paradise and deliverance from Pharaoh and wrongdoing people; refuge for home and self.
Rabbanā innanā āmannā fa-ghfir lanā dhunūbanā wa qinā 'adhāban-nār — plea for forgiveness and protection from the punishment of the Fire.
'Rabbanā ātinā fi'd-dunyā ḥasanah wa fi'l-ākhirati ḥasanah' — the most comprehensive Qur'anic dua for good in this life (including provision) and the next.
Mūsā's dua after watering the flocks: 'Rabbi innī limā anzalta ilayya min khayrin faqīr' — a humble plea for provision when in need of work and sustenance.
'Qul allāhumma mālika'l-mulk... bi-yadika'l-khayr' — declaring Allah as Owner of all sovereignty in whose hand is all good; recited seeking honor, provision, and success.
'Allāhumma-kfinī bi-ḥalālika ʿan ḥarāmika wa aghninī bi-faḍlika ʿamman siwāk' — the Prophet's dua for sufficiency through lawful provision (Tirmidhī 3563).
'Allāhumma innī as'aluka ʿilman nāfiʿan wa rizqan ṭayyiban wa ʿamalan mutaqabbalā' — asking for beneficial knowledge, good provision, and accepted deeds (Ibn Mājah 925).
'Rabbi zidnī ʿilmā' — the quintessential Qur'anic dua for increase in knowledge; the go-to supplication of students.
Mūsā's dua 'Rabbi-shraḥ lī ṣadrī' — expand my chest, ease my task, and loosen my tongue; recited for ease in learning, teaching, and speaking clearly.
'Rabbanā lā tuzigh qulūbanā baʿda idh hadaytanā' — asking that hearts not deviate after guidance and for mercy; a plea for firmness upon knowledge and truth.
'Ihdinā aṣ-ṣirāṭ al-mustaqīm' — the daily prayer for guidance to the straight path, foundational to seeking wisdom in all affairs.
'Rabbi adkhilnī mudkhala ṣidqin wa akhrijnī mukhraja ṣidq' — asking for a truthful entrance and exit and a helping authority; recited for integrity and support in one's undertakings.
'Rabbanā hab lanā min azwājinā wa dhurriyyātinā qurrata aʿyun wajʿalnā li'l-muttaqīna imāmā' — the dua of the servants of the Merciful to be made leaders/examples for the righteous.
Sulaymān's dua 'Rabbi awziʿnī an ashkura niʿmataka allatī anʿamta ʿalayya wa an aʿmala ṣāliḥan tarḍāh' — enable me to be grateful and to do righteous deeds You are pleased with.
'Rabbi awziʿnī an ashkura niʿmataka... wa aṣliḥ lī fī dhurriyyatī' — gratitude for blessings, righteous action, and betterment in one's family and offspring.

'Allāhumma innī aʿūdhu bika mina'l-hammi wa'l-ḥazani wa'l-ʿajzi wa'l-kasali... wa ḍalaʿi'd-dayn' — refuge from anxiety, incapacity, laziness, and debt; the Prophet's dua for productivity and relief in livelihood (Bukhārī 6369).
Duʿāʾ upon waking — 'Alḥamdulillāhil-ladhī aḥyānā baʿda mā amātanā wa ilayhin-nushūr' (praise to Allah who gave us life after death); Bukhārī 6312. The very first dua of the daily routine.

Mūsā's dua 'Rabbi-shraḥ lī ṣadrī wa yassir lī amrī' (expand my chest, ease my task, untie my tongue) — the classic supplication recited before a difficult task, speech, exam or presentation. Spans 20:25-28.
'Rabbi zidnī ʿilman' (My Lord, increase me in knowledge) — the beloved dua for the start of study or seeking knowledge; brings mindfulness to learning.
Duʿāʾ upon leaving the home — 'Bismillāh, tawakkaltu ʿalallāh, wa lā ḥawla wa lā quwwata illā billāh' (in Allah's name, I trust in Allah); Abū Dāwūd 5095, Tirmidhī 3426.
Duʿāʾ before eating — saying 'Bismillāh' (and if forgotten, 'Bismillāhi awwalahu wa ākhirahu'); Abū Dāwūd 3767, Tirmidhī 1858. Brings mindfulness to every meal.
Duʿāʾ after eating — 'Alḥamdulillāhil-ladhī aṭʿamanī hādhā wa razaqanīhi min ghayri ḥawlin minnī wa lā quwwah' (praise to Allah who fed me this and provided it); Abū Dāwūd 4023, Tirmidhī 3458.
Duʿāʾ before sleep — 'Bismika Allāhumma amūtu wa aḥyā' (in Your name, O Allah, I die and I live); Bukhārī 6324, Muslim 2711.
Duʿāʾ entering the home — mentioning Allah's name on entering so Shayṭān has no lodging or share of the meal; Muslim 2018. A moment of mindfulness at the threshold.

The Qur'anic dua of mounting/riding — 'Subḥānal-ladhī sakhkhara lanā hādhā wa mā kunnā lahu muqrinīn, wa innā ilā rabbinā la-munqalibūn' (Glory to Him who subjected this to us). Recited on boarding any vehicle. Spans 43:13-14.
The full Duʿāʾ as-safar (travel supplication) — 'Allāhumma innā nasʾaluka fī safarinā hādhā al-birra wat-taqwā...' (we ask You in this journey for righteousness and piety); Muslim 1342.

Duʿāʾ when stopping at a place / arriving somewhere new — 'Aʿūdhu bi-kalimātillāhit-tāmmāti min sharri mā khalaq' (I seek refuge in Allah's perfect words from the evil of what He created); Muslim 2708.

'Rabbi aʿūdhu bika min hamazātish-shayāṭīn, wa aʿūdhu bika rabbi an yaḥḍurūn' (I seek refuge in You from the whispers of devils and from their presence) — a Qur'anic refuge for everyday moments. Spans 23:97-98.
Sayyid al-Istighfār (the master supplication for forgiveness) — 'Allāhumma anta rabbī lā ilāha illā anta, khalaqtanī wa anā ʿabduka...'; said morning and evening; Bukhārī 6306.

Morning/evening protection dua — 'Bismillāhil-ladhī lā yaḍurru maʿa-smihi shayʾun fil-arḍi wa lā fis-samāʾ, wa huwas-samīʿul-ʿalīm' (in Allah's name, with whose name nothing on earth or heaven can harm); Abū Dāwūd 5088, Tirmidhī 3388.
Refuge from anxiety and daily burdens — 'Allāhumma innī aʿūdhu bika minal-hammi wal-ḥazan, wal-ʿajzi wal-kasal...' (from worry, grief, incapacity and laziness); Bukhārī 6369.
